summary.title: Systems Performance: Enterprise and the Cloud, 2nd Edition (2020)
summary.one_liner: Learn systems performance methodology first (models, architecture, USE Method), then apply it with Linux observability tools such as perf, Ftrace, BPF, bpftrace, and BCC.
takeaways: Systems performance covers application, OS, kernel, and hardware performance, with goals of improving price/performance and reducing latency outliers.
The book teaches durable skills first (models, architecture, methodologies) before implementation with tools and tuning.
Methodologies such as the USE Method are a central focus, giving a starting point for performance investigations.
Linux is the primary example OS; the 2nd edition adds BPF, BCC, bpftrace, perf, and Ftrace and removes most Solaris content.
The draft is roughly 800 pages; the book is aimed at sysadmins, SREs, and performance engineers in enterprise and cloud settings.
summary.summary: This is the official homepage for Brendan Gregg's book Systems Performance: Enterprise and the Cloud, 2nd Edition (Addison-Wesley, 2020). The page outlines what changed from the first edition, the book's audience, its table of contents (from Intro and Methodology through CPUs, memory, file systems, disks, networking, cloud computing, benchmarking, and perf, Ftrace, BPF chapters, plus a case study), and links to purchase options, related content, and errata. The book's distinguishing approach is to combine many performance methodologies with OS-agnostic concepts and then use Linux as the main worked example.
